intent.raw_query: Patagonia hiking Torres del Paine, $4500, 12 days, December 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Torres del Paine, Patagonia

experiences.name: W Trek Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic W Trek, a 4-5 day trekking route through the heart of Torres del Paine National Park. The trail covers approximately 80km and passes through stunning valleys, glaciers, and viewpoints including the base of the Torres, the French Valley, and Grey Glacier. Book refugios or campsites in advance as spots fill up quickly during peak season.
experiences.location: Torres del Paine National Park, Central Circuit

experiences.name: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Wake before dawn and hike the 4-5 hour trail to the iconic granite towers of Torres del Paine. Arriving at sunrise rewards trekkers with breathtaking golden light reflecting off the turquoise lagoon at the base of the three towering peaks. This is considered one of the most spectacular viewpoints in all of Patagonia and a bucket-list moment for any nature lover.
experiences.location: Mirador Las Torres, Eastern Sector, Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition
experiences.description: Paddle through the icy waters of Lago Grey surrounded by floating icebergs calved from the massive Grey Glacier. A guided kayaking tour brings you up close to the stunning blue ice formations and offers a unique water-level perspective of the glacier that trekkers on foot simply cannot experience. Guides provide all equipment and safety briefings.
experiences.location: Lago Grey, Grey Glacier Sector, Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Valle del Francés Day Trek
experiences.description: Hike into the dramatic French Valley, a glacially carved amphitheater surrounded by hanging glaciers, jagged peaks, and cascading waterfalls. The trail ascends through lenga beech forests and opens into panoramic views of Paine Grande and the Cuernos del Paine. Wildlife sightings including condors, guanacos, and Andean foxes are common along this route.
experiences.location: Valle del Francés, Central Sector, Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Traditional Patagonian Asado Dinner
experiences.description: After days of trekking, reward yourself with an authentic Patagonian asado featuring slow-roasted lamb cooked on an open wood fire, a centuries-old tradition of the region's gauchos. Local estancias and lodges near the park serve this cultural culinary experience paired with Chilean Carménère wine. It is a deeply rooted cultural tradition that connects visitors to the rugged heritage of Patagonian ranch life.
experiences.location: Estancia Cerro Guido, Puerto Natales Gateway Area, Patagonia

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Torres del Paine, Patagonia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 22:30. Collect luggage, arrange pre-booked budget transfer or shared shuttle to Puerto Natales (approx. 1.5 hrs). Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort, Torres del Paine. Grab a light snack if available at the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport snacks
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food court
meals.dinner: Light snack from a convenience store or vending machine near the airport/accommodation upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book a shared shuttle from the airport to Puerto Natales to save costs (approx. $15-25 USD). Have local Chilean pesos ready. Confirm check-in arrangements with Aegean Bliss Resort in advance since arrival is late at night. Pack a light carry-on snack for the journey.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a late breakfast, visit the Puerto Natales town center on foot. Explore the waterfront Costanera promenade along Última Esperanza Sound, enjoy the views of the mountains and fjords, and get oriented with the area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Museo Histórico Municipal de Puerto Natales to learn about the region's history and indigenous Kawésqar people. Stop by local gear rental shops to rent or check trekking equipment needed for upcoming hikes in Torres del Paine. Buy groceries and supplies from a local supermarket (Unimarc or similar) to stock up on budget-friendly trail snacks, instant meals, and water.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll the main street Arturo Prat in Puerto Natales, browse local artisan shops for souvenirs. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at a local budget restaurant and plan the upcoming trek days.

meals.breakfast: Included at Aegean Bliss Resort or prepare simple breakfast from grocery store supplies (bread, jam, instant coffee)
meals.lunch: Empanadas or a cheap set lunch (menú del día) at a local café in Puerto Natales (~$5-8 USD)
meals.dinner: Budget restaurant in Puerto Natales such as Mesita Grande or a local comedor offering a fixed-price dinner (~$10-12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to fully rest and prepare for the strenuous days ahead. Confirm your park entry permit for Torres del Paine online via CONAF website if not already done (park entry ~$35 USD in peak season). Stock up on food supplies here as prices inside the park are significantly higher.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from Puerto Natales via public bus or shared shuttle to Torres del Paine National Park (approx. 2.5 hrs, ~$10-15 USD). Arrive at park entrance, pay entry fee, and head to the Laguna Amarga ranger station. Begin a moderate afternoon hike to Laguna Amarga viewpoint to admire the flamingo-filled lagoon with the Torres del Paine massif as a backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking the trail toward Hotel Las Torres area. Explore the banks of Río Paine and enjoy views of the surrounding lenga beech forests. Take photos at the Cascada Paine waterfall viewpoint accessible along the trail. Return to the campsite or accommodation area by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Set up camp at Camping Torres or check into the nearest budget refugio. Prepare a hot meal at the campsite cooking area. Attend any ranger-led orientation talk if available. Rest and prepare gear for the big hike tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Prepare oatmeal, fruit, and instant coffee at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from Puerto Natales supplies eaten on the trail (sandwiches, nuts, energy bars)
meals.dinner: Self-cooked meal at campsite (pasta with canned sauce, instant soup) or budget refugio dinner if included

day_by_day.notes: Book camping spots or refugio bunks in Torres del Paine well in advance through CONAF or Vertice Patagonia/Fantastico Sur websites — peak December slots fill up months ahead. Bring all camping gear or rent in Puerto Natales. Water from park streams is generally safe to drink after filtering.

day_by_day.morning: MIRADOR LAS TORRES SUNRISE HIKE: Wake at 4:00 AM and begin the iconic 4-5 hour hike to the base of the granite Torres del Paine towers. Start from Camping Torres or Hotel Las Torres trailhead. Hike through lenga beech forest, cross a suspension bridge, and ascend the steep moraine field to reach Mirador Las Torres at sunrise. Witness the towers glowing gold and orange in the early morning light — the highlight of the entire trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to the trailhead (approx. 2-3 hrs). Rest and have a substantial lunch at the campsite. Spend the afternoon recovering, washing gear, journaling, or taking short nature walks near the campsite to spot guanacos, condors, and Andean foxes.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate completing the iconic hike with a slightly more indulgent campsite meal. Share stories with fellow trekkers at the campsite. Early bedtime to recover for the next day's trek.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed energy bars, trail mix, and instant coffee consumed before or during the early hike
meals.lunch: Substantial packed meal back at camp after descent (canned tuna, crackers, dried fruit, hot soup)
meals.dinner: Self-cooked hearty campsite dinner (rice with lentils, instant mashed potatoes, hot chocolate)

day_by_day.notes: This is the most physically demanding day of the trip. The round-trip hike is approximately 18-20 km with 800m elevation gain. Start no later than 4:30 AM to catch the sunrise. Bring headlamps, warm layers, waterproof jacket, trekking poles, and at least 2 liters of water. Weather can change rapidly — be prepared for wind and cold even in December.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the campsite. Sleep in, have a leisurely breakfast, and do light stretching. Take a gentle walk along the banks of Lago Nordenskjöld to enjoy the turquoise glacial waters and mountain reflections. Spot wildlife including guanacos and Magellanic woodpeckers in the surrounding forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the short trail to Mirador Cuernos (approx. 3-4 hrs round trip, moderate difficulty) for dramatic views of the jagged Cuernos del Paine peaks reflected in Lago Nordenskjöld. The distinctive two-toned rock formations of the Cuernos are one of Patagonia's most photographed sights.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp by late afternoon. Cook dinner and spend the evening stargazing — Torres del Paine offers exceptional dark skies. Look for the Milky Way and Southern Cross constellation. Chat with fellow trekkers from around the world.

meals.breakfast: Oatmeal with powdered milk and dried fruit, instant coffee or tea at campsite
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail (energy bars, peanut butter crackers, dried mango)
meals.dinner: Campsite pasta with olive oil, garlic powder, and parmesan (lightweight and calorie-dense)

day_by_day.notes: This is a lighter day designed for recovery after the Torres hike. The Mirador Cuernos trail is well-marked. Keep an eye out for the park's famous wildlife — pumas are occasionally spotted in this area, especially at dawn and dusk. Always maintain safe distances from all wildlife.

day_by_day.morning: Pack up camp and trek toward Campamento Italiano, the gateway to Valle del Francés. Hike along the shores of Lago Nordenskjöld on the well-marked W Trek trail (approx. 4-5 hrs). The trail offers continuous spectacular views of the lake and surrounding peaks. Arrive at Campamento Italiano (free camping) by midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drop heavy packs at Campamento Italiano and begin the VALLE DEL FRANCÉS DAY TREK with a lighter daypack. Hike up into the dramatic French Valley — a glacially carved amphitheater surrounded by hanging glaciers, soaring granite walls, and cascading waterfalls. Listen for the thunderous crack of ice calving from the glaciers above. Hike to Mirador Británico for the best panoramic views of the valley (approx. 3-4 hrs round trip from camp).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Campamento Italiano by early evening. Set up tents at the free campsite. Cook a warm meal and reflect on the breathtaking Valle del Francés experience. Rest well for the next day.

meals.breakfast: Quick campsite breakfast before packing up — instant oatmeal and energy bars
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten in Valle del Francés with a view of hanging glaciers (sandwiches, nuts, chocolate)
meals.dinner: Campsite dinner at Campamento Italiano — instant rice with dehydrated vegetables and soy sauce

day_by_day.notes: Campamento Italiano is a free CONAF campsite with basic facilities. The Valle del Francés hike is approximately 8-10 km round trip from the campsite with moderate-to-challenging terrain. Watch for falling rocks and ice near the valley walls. This is one of the most spectacular sections of the W Trek and should not be rushed.

day_by_day.morning: Hike from Campamento Italiano toward Refugio Grey along the W Trek trail (approx. 5-6 hrs). Pass through diverse landscapes including lenga beech forests, open pampas, and rocky shorelines along Lago Grey. Enjoy views of the Grey Glacier peeking into the lake from a distance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the Grey Glacier viewpoint area. Walk to the free lakeside viewpoint to see the massive Grey Glacier up close — a stunning wall of blue ice calving into the steel-grey lake. Icebergs of various sizes float in the lake, creating a surreal Arctic landscape. Spend time photographing and absorbing the spectacle.
day_by_day.evening: Set up camp at Camping Grey (pre-booked). Cook dinner and enjoy the long Patagonian summer evening light — in December, daylight lasts until nearly 10:30 PM. Watch the glacier glow in the evening light. Rest for the return journey.

meals.breakfast: Campsite breakfast at Campamento Italiano before departure — oatmeal and instant coffee
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch eaten with views of Lago Grey (crackers with peanut butter, energy gels, dried fruit)
meals.dinner: Hot campsite meal at Camping Grey — lentil soup with bread and hot tea

day_by_day.notes: The Grey Glacier is one of the largest glaciers in Patagonia outside of Antarctica. Do not attempt to walk on or near the glacier without a licensed guide. Camping Grey has paid facilities (~$15-20 USD per person). The trail from Italiano to Grey is one of the longer daily segments of the W Trek — pace yourself and stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Wake early for a final sunrise view of Grey Glacier before breaking camp. Begin the return hike back along the W Trek toward the park administration area at Pudeto or Lago Pehoé (approx. 5-6 hrs). The return trail offers different perspectives of the landscapes already traversed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Lago Pehoé and take the catamaran ferry across to Pudeto (approx. $30 USD, runs a few times daily — check schedule in advance). From Pudeto, take the park bus or arranged shuttle back toward Puerto Natales. Arrive in Puerto Natales by late afternoon. Check back into Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate completing the W Trek with a well-deserved restaurant dinner in Puerto Natales. Take a hot shower, do laundry, and rest in a proper bed. Reflect on the incredible week of hiking.

meals.breakfast: Final campsite breakfast at Camping Grey — remaining trail food supplies
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the return trail or a quick bite at the Pudeto kiosk while waiting for the catamaran
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a sit-down dinner at a local Puerto Natales restaurant — try Aldea Restaurant or El Living for budget-friendly options (~$12-15 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm catamaran ferry times in advance as schedules vary by season. The ferry booking can be made at the Lago Pehoé dock or pre-booked online. After 6 days of camping, a hot shower and restaurant meal will feel like a luxury. This is a good time to recharge devices, update travel journals, and plan the remaining days.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery day in Puerto Natales. Sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and take care of any personal needs — laundry, gear drying, resupplying. Take a leisurely walk along the Costanera waterfront to watch fishing boats and enjoy the mountain views across the sound.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional: Visit Cueva del Milodón Natural Monument (approx. 24 km from Puerto Natales, accessible by local bus or hitchhiking — very common in Patagonia). This prehistoric cave housed a giant ground sloth (Mylodon) and offers fascinating geological formations and a short nature trail (~$10 USD entry). Alternatively, explore more of Puerto Natales town and visit local craft markets.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Puerto Natales evening scene. Visit a local craft beer bar such as Baguales Brewery for a Patagonian craft beer (budget 1-2 drinks). Prepare for the final days of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort or local café — eggs, bread, fresh juice
meals.lunch: Menú del día (set lunch) at a local restaurant in Puerto Natales — soup, main course, and drink (~$7-9 USD)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using supermarket ingredients at the resort, or grab takeaway empanadas and sopaipillas from a local bakery (~$3-5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: This is a well-deserved recovery day. Your body will need rest after the multi-day W Trek. Hitchhiking (dedo) is culturally accepted and common in Patagonia — many budget travelers use it to reach Cueva del Milodón and other nearby sites. Always use common sense and travel in pairs when hitchhiking.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Eve day trip: Take an early morning bus or shared van back into Torres del Paine National Park for a day visit (no overnight camping required). Head to the Salto Grande waterfall — a powerful cascade connecting Lago Nordenskjöld and Lago Pehoé, accessible via a short 20-minute walk from the Pudeto dock. The roaring waterfall framed by the Cuernos peaks is one of the park's most accessible and spectacular sights.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Mirador Pehoé trail (approx. 2 hrs round trip) for panoramic views of Lago Pehoé, the Cuernos, and the Torres in the distance. Spot flamingos wading in the shallow lake margins. Return to the Pudeto area and take the afternoon bus back to Puerto Natales, arriving by early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve celebration in Puerto Natales. Join locals for the festive atmosphere — Chilean Christmas Eve (Nochebuena) is the main celebration. Many restaurants offer special holiday menus. Enjoy a festive dinner and the warm community spirit of a small Patagonian town celebrating the holidays.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — bread, cheese, instant coffee
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch eaten at Salto Grande or Mirador Pehoé viewpoint
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner at a local Puerto Natales restaurant — many offer a fixed Nochebuena menu (~$15-18 USD, slightly splurge-worthy for the occasion)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve in Chilean Patagonia is a wonderful cultural experience. Locals gather with family and there is often a festive atmosphere in town. Some restaurants may be fully booked — make a reservation in advance. The Salto Grande and Mirador Pehoé area is one of the most accessible and rewarding day-trip destinations in the park.

day_by_day.morning: Feliz Navidad! Christmas Day relaxation morning. Enjoy a slow start with a special breakfast. Take a peaceful morning walk along the Puerto Natales waterfront, watching the sunrise over the Última Esperanza Sound. Reflect on the incredible natural experiences of the past 10 days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional half-day kayaking or boat tour on Última Esperanza Sound departing from Puerto Natales (budget operators available, ~$25-35 USD). Paddle past dramatic fjord scenery, spot black-necked swans, cormorants, and sea lions. Alternatively, take a free self-guided hike on Cerro Dorotea, a hill behind Puerto Natales offering panoramic views of the town, sound, and mountains (approx. 3 hrs round trip, free access).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in the Patagonia region. Pack bags and prepare for departure. Enjoy a final budget dinner in Puerto Natales, sharing travel stories with fellow adventurers met along the W Trek. Toast to an unforgettable journey.

meals.breakfast: Special Christmas breakfast — treat yourself to a café con leche and medialunas (croissants) at a local bakery or café
meals.lunch: Light lunch from a supermarket or local café — fresh bread, avocado, and local cheese
meals.dinner: Final farewell dinner at a favorite Puerto Natales restaurant — try the local lamb (cordero) dish, a Patagonian specialty (~$12-15 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Many businesses in Puerto Natales may be closed or have reduced hours on Christmas Day. Plan meals and activities accordingly. Cerro Dorotea is a free and highly rewarding alternative activity if boat tours are unavailable. Begin packing and organizing gear for the return journey. Donate or sell any unwanted camping gear to fellow travelers or local hostels.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Patagonia. Wake early, have a last breakfast, and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Arrange shared shuttle or bus transfer from Puerto Natales to Punta Arenas airport (approx. 3-4 hrs, ~$15-20 USD). Enjoy the final views of the Patagonian steppe, guanacos grazing alongside the road, and the vast open skies as you travel north.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Punta Arenas airport with ample time before departure. Browse the small airport shops for any last-minute souvenirs — locally made woolen goods and Patagonian chocolates make great budget gifts. Reflect on 12 extraordinary days of hiking, trekking, and wilderness exploration in one of the world's most remote and spectacular landscapes.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Punta Arenas. Carry memories of the Torres del Paine granite towers, the turquoise glacial lakes, the roaring Salto Grande, and the vast blue ice of Grey Glacier — experiences that will last a lifetime.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort or a quick café stop in Puerto Natales before the shuttle
meals.lunch: Airport café or packed snacks from the supermarket for the journey
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Book the shuttle from Puerto Natales to Punta Arenas well in advance, especially during the busy December holiday period. Allow at least 4-4.5 hours before your flight for the transfer. Keep essential documents, camera gear, and valuables in your carry-on. Budget summary tip: The total trip cost for 12 days can be kept between $600-900 USD (excluding flights) by using shared shuttles, camping, self-cooking, and free park trails.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in Torres del Paine. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest to prepare for the adventure ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A - travel day
meals.lunch: N/A - travel day
meals.dinner: Light snack available at resort upon arrival or grab a quick bite at the airport before boarding your transfer.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your airport transfer with the resort in advance. Pack a light snack in your carry-on for the late arrival. Confirm gear and hiking boots are accessible in your luggage for early morning use the next day.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast with views of the Patagonian landscape. Spend the morning orienting yourself — visit the resort's information desk to pick up trail maps, confirm W Trek logistics, and rent or check any gear you may need.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle orientation walk around the resort grounds and nearby shoreline to acclimate to the altitude and wind. Explore the beachfront area, spot local birdlife including Andean condors and black-necked swans, and soak in your first panoramic views of the park.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a brief park orientation session if available at the resort or nearby visitor center. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at the resort restaurant, review your itinerary, and prepare your pack for the coming days of trekking.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — eggs, cold cuts, fresh bread, and local jams
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at the resort café — try a hearty Patagonian lamb sandwich or vegetable soup
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant dinner — grilled salmon or local lamb stew with a glass of Chilean Carménère wine (~$25-35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to fully recover from jet lag. Stock up on trail snacks, energy bars, and water purification tablets at the resort shop or in Puerto Natales if possible. Check weather forecasts for the week ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the W Trek — Day 1: Head to the Mirador Las Torres trailhead. Start the 4-5 hour ascent early to beat crowds. The trail winds through lenga beech forests and glacial moraine before the final steep boulder scramble to the iconic granite towers. Aim to arrive at the mirador by mid-morning for the best light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend time at the base of the towers soaking in the dramatic scenery — three massive granite spires reflected in the turquoise glacial lake below. Begin your descent back down the trail, taking your time to enjoy the forest and wildlife on the way down.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Refugio Las Torres or camp at the base area. Settle in, dry your gear, and rest your legs. Share stories with fellow trekkers around the common area.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast from the resort or Refugio Las Torres — oatmeal, fruit, and coffee before the ascent
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch on the mountain — energy bars, nuts, dried fruit, cheese, and crackers
meals.dinner: Hot meal at Refugio Las Torres — three-course set menu featuring soup, pasta or rice dish, and dessert (~$30-40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is the most iconic hike in the park — start as early as 6:00 AM for sunrise conditions. Dress in layers as weather can change rapidly. Trekking poles are strongly recommended for the boulder field near the top. Book refugio accommodation and meals in advance.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek — Day 2: Wake before dawn for the Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike. Re-ascend the trail in darkness with headlamps to reach the mirador just as the first golden light strikes the towers, creating the famous 'alpen glow' effect on the granite peaks — one of Patagonia's most breathtaking spectacles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and continue the W Trek westward toward Valle del Francés. Trek through the central valley, crossing suspension bridges over glacial rivers. Arrive at Campamento Italiano at the entrance to the French Valley.
day_by_day.evening: Set up camp or check into Refugio Los Cuernos nearby. Enjoy the dramatic views of the Cuernos del Paine (Horns of Paine) turning orange and pink at sunset. Rest and prepare for the French Valley day ahead.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed breakfast eaten before the predawn ascent — energy bars, banana, and thermos coffee
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch at Campamento Italiano — peanut butter wraps, trail mix, and fruit
meals.dinner: Dinner at Refugio Los Cuernos — hearty beef or vegetable stew with bread and hot tea (~$30-40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The sunrise hike requires a 3:00-4:00 AM wake-up. Bring a headlamp with fresh batteries and warm layers as pre-dawn temperatures can drop significantly even in December. The second ascent is worth every step for the magical light show.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek — Day 3: Valle del Francés Day Trek. Leave packs at Campamento Italiano and embark on the dramatic French Valley hike. Ascend through ancient beech forest into a glacially carved amphitheater. Listen for the thunderous crack of ice breaking from hanging glaciers on the valley walls above.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue up to Mirador Británico (the upper viewpoint) for a stunning 360-degree panorama of glaciers, peaks, and the valley below. On clear days you can see Lago Nordenskjöld, Lago Pehoé, and the main peaks of the massif simultaneously. Descend back to Campamento Italiano and collect your packs.
day_by_day.evening: Continue trekking west to Refugio Paine Grande on the shore of Lago Pehoé. Check in, shower if facilities allow, and relax on the deck watching the sunset over the lake and glaciers.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Refugio Los Cuernos before departing — eggs, toast, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch in the French Valley — sandwiches, cheese, and chocolate
meals.dinner: Dinner at Refugio Paine Grande — pasta with meat sauce or vegetarian option, soup starter (~$28-38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The French Valley round trip adds approximately 6-8 hours to your day — start early. The valley is known for rockfall and iceberg calving sounds — a truly wild and immersive experience. Weather in the valley can be dramatically different from the main trail.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek — Day 4: Grey Glacier Sector. Trek westward from Refugio Paine Grande along the northern shore of Lago Grey toward the Grey Glacier. The trail offers increasingly dramatic views of the glacier tongue and floating blue icebergs in the lake below.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Mirador Grey for close-up views of the massive glacier face. The Grey Glacier is one of the largest in Patagonia outside Antarctica — a wall of blue ice stretching kilometers wide. Spend time at the viewpoint before beginning the return trek to Refugio Paine Grande.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Refugio Paine Grande for your final night on the W Trek. Celebrate completing the iconic route with fellow trekkers. Enjoy a well-earned hot shower and a hearty dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Refugio Paine Grande — porridge, toast, eggs, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the glacier trail — crackers, cheese, nuts, and dried mango
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at Refugio Paine Grande — lamb or salmon main course with Chilean wine (~$35-45 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Grey Glacier trail is approximately 11km each way — this is a full and demanding day. Wear sunscreen as glacier reflection intensifies UV exposure. Icebergs in the lake range from small chunks to house-sized formations — all a stunning electric blue.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek — Day 5 / Return: Take the early catamaran ferry across Lago Pehoé from Refugio Paine Grande back toward the park entrance. The 30-minute boat ride offers spectacular final views of the Cuernos del Paine and surrounding peaks from the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer back to Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon arrival, check back in, unpack, do laundry, and take a long hot shower. Rest your legs with a gentle walk along the beachfront or simply relax on your room's terrace with a book and a glass of wine.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a proper sit-down dinner at the resort restaurant to celebrate completing the W Trek. Reflect on the week's highlights over a quality meal.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Refugio Paine Grande before the ferry — toast, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a restaurant near the park entrance or packed meal during transfer — empanadas or a warm soup
meals.dinner: Special dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant — grilled Patagonian lamb chops with chimichurri, roasted vegetables, and a bottle of Carménère (~$40-55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the catamaran ferry in advance as it fills up quickly. The ferry schedule is typically twice daily — confirm current times with the refugio. This is a well-deserved rest day after 5 days of trekking.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery day. Sleep in, enjoy a long resort breakfast, and spend the morning at leisure. Use the resort's amenities — whether a pool, spa treatment, or simply lounging with views of the Patagonian landscape. Let your legs fully recover.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle afternoon activity: take a scenic drive or guided resort excursion to Lago Sarmiento or the Laguna Azul area in the lesser-visited northeastern sector of the park. These areas offer beautiful flamingo-spotting opportunities and tranquil landscapes without demanding hikes.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the Traditional Patagonian Asado Dinner experience. Gather around an open fire as a gaucho-style asado featuring slow-roasted lamb on a cross (asado al palo) is prepared over several hours. Enjoy the communal atmosphere with wine, salads, and traditional sides under the Patagonian sky.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full buffet breakfast at the resort — take your time and enjoy multiple courses
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort café or packed for the afternoon excursion — fresh salad, soup, and crusty bread
meals.dinner: Traditional Patagonian Asado Dinner experience — slow-roasted whole lamb, chimichurri, roasted vegetables, empanadas, and Chilean red wine (~$55-75 per person, experience included)

day_by_day.notes: The Patagonian Asado is a cultural highlight not to be missed. Book in advance as spots are limited. This evening experience typically lasts 3-4 hours and includes storytelling about gaucho culture and Patagonian traditions.

day_by_day.morning: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition — Morning session. Meet your guide at the Lago Grey launch point and receive a safety briefing and paddling instruction. Set out on the glassy waters of Lago Grey, navigating through floating icebergs calved from the massive Grey Glacier. The scale of the ice formations is awe-inspiring from water level.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the kayaking expedition, paddling closer to the glacier face than any hiking trail allows. Listen to the glacier creak and crack, and watch for calving events. Return to shore and warm up with hot drinks provided by guides. Transfer back to the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort. Visit the resort bar for a pisco sour — Chile's iconic cocktail — and watch the long Patagonian sunset (which in December can last until 10:30 PM). Enjoy a casual dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before the kayaking departure — eggs, toast, fruit, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by the kayaking operator or eaten at the Lago Grey area — sandwiches and hot soup
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at the resort or nearby restaurant — Patagonian king crab (centolla) pasta or lamb burger (~$25-35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The kayaking expedition typically runs 4-6 hours total. Waterproof gear and dry bags are provided but wear warm thermal layers underneath. December weather can still be cold on the water. This experience offers a completely different perspective of the glacier than hiking.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Eve exploration: Hike to Mirador Nordenskjöld for panoramic views of Lago Nordenskjöld and the Cuernos del Paine — a moderately easy trail offering some of the most photogenic views in the park without the crowds of the main W Trek routes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort and spend the afternoon at leisure. Browse the resort gift shop for locally made Patagonian crafts, wool goods, and artisan products to bring home as gifts. Write postcards, edit photos, or simply relax by the water.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve celebration dinner at the resort. Many Patagonian lodges offer a special holiday menu — expect traditional Chilean and Patagonian specialties alongside festive touches. Enjoy the unique experience of celebrating Christmas with views of glaciers and mountains under a long summer evening sky.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — treat yourself to the full spread including fresh pastries and local honey
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch on the Nordenskjöld trail — cheese, crackers, fruit, and chocolate
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — holiday set menu with local seafood, lamb, and a festive dessert with sparkling wine (~$50-70 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm with the resort whether they offer a special Christmas Eve dinner and book your spot in advance. The long summer days in Patagonia mean you can hike until 9:00 PM if needed — take advantage of the extraordinary golden hour light.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day: Enjoy a special Christmas morning sleep-in and a festive resort breakfast. Spend the morning at your own pace — whether that's a gentle stroll along the beachfront, wildlife watching for guanacos, foxes, and condors near the resort, or simply reading on your terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional half-day guided nature walk with a local naturalist guide. Explore the unique Magellanic steppe ecosystem around the resort, learning about local flora, fauna, and the geological history of Patagonia. This low-intensity experience is perfect for resting legs after the W Trek while still engaging with the natural environment.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening in Torres del Paine. Enjoy a sunset walk along the shoreline, then gather for a special Christmas dinner. Toast to an unforgettable trip with a bottle of Chilean sparkling wine and reflect on the incredible landscapes, wildlife, and experiences of the past 12 days.

meals.breakfast: Festive Christmas breakfast at the resort — special holiday spread with fresh pastries, smoked salmon, and champagne mimosas
meals.lunch: Relaxed Christmas lunch at the resort restaurant — roast chicken, salads, and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Christmas dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — special holiday menu featuring the best of Patagonian cuisine — king crab, slow-roasted lamb, and a traditional Chilean dessert like leche asada (~$55-75 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day in Patagonia is a magical experience — the long summer light, dramatic scenery, and festive atmosphere at the resort create an unforgettable holiday memory. Confirm Christmas dinner reservations well in advance as these fill up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Patagonia. Wake early for one last sunrise walk along the beachfront or a short stroll to a nearby viewpoint to say goodbye to the towers and peaks. Pack your bags, do a final gear check, and ensure all souvenirs are safely packed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and begin the transfer toward Puerto Natales or Punta Arenas for your departure flight. If time allows before your transfer, stop at a local shop in Puerto Natales for last-minute souvenirs — Patagonian wool products, local chocolates, and artisan crafts make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport. Reflect on an extraordinary 12-day journey through one of the world's most spectacular wilderness destinations — the W Trek, glacier kayaking, sunrise at the towers, and the warmth of Patagonian hospitality will stay with you long after you return home.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — enjoy every last bite of the Patagonian spread before checkout
meals.lunch: Lunch at a recommended restaurant in Puerto Natales during transfer stop — try Afrigonia or El Living for excellent mid-range dining (~$15-25 per person)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight dining depending on departure time — pick up local snacks and a bottle of Chilean wine at the airport duty-free as a final Patagonian memento

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3-4 hours for the transfer from Torres del Paine to Punta Arenas airport. Road conditions can vary and the drive is long. Confirm your transfer booking the evening before. Carry all valuables and documents in your hand luggage. Punta Arenas airport has limited dining options so eat before arriving if possible.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Torres del Paine, Patagonia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Torres del Paine, Patagonia

experiences.name: W Trek Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic W Trek, a 4-5 day trekking route through the heart of Torres del Paine National Park. The trail covers approximately 80km and passes through stunning valleys, glaciers, and viewpoints including the base of the Torres, the French Valley, and Grey Glacier. Book refugios or campsites in advance as spots fill up quickly during peak season.
experiences.location: Torres del Paine National Park, Central Circuit

experiences.name: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Wake before dawn and hike the 4-5 hour trail to the iconic granite towers of Torres del Paine. Arriving at sunrise rewards trekkers with breathtaking golden light reflecting off the turquoise lagoon at the base of the three towering peaks. This is considered one of the most spectacular viewpoints in all of Patagonia and a bucket-list moment for any nature lover.
experiences.location: Mirador Las Torres, Eastern Sector, Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition
experiences.description: Paddle through the icy waters of Lago Grey surrounded by floating icebergs calved from the massive Grey Glacier. A guided kayaking tour brings you up close to the stunning blue ice formations and offers a unique water-level perspective of the glacier that trekkers on foot simply cannot experience. Guides provide all equipment and safety briefings.
experiences.location: Lago Grey, Grey Glacier Sector, Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Valle del Francés Day Trek
experiences.description: Hike into the dramatic French Valley, a glacially carved amphitheater surrounded by hanging glaciers, jagged peaks, and cascading waterfalls. The trail ascends through lenga beech forests and opens into panoramic views of Paine Grande and the Cuernos del Paine. Wildlife sightings including condors, guanacos, and Andean foxes are common along this route.
experiences.location: Valle del Francés, Central Sector, Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Traditional Patagonian Asado Dinner
experiences.description: After days of trekking, reward yourself with an authentic Patagonian asado featuring slow-roasted lamb cooked on an open wood fire, a centuries-old tradition of the region's gauchos. Local estancias and lodges near the park serve this cultural culinary experience paired with Chilean Carménère wine. It is a deeply rooted cultural tradition that connects visitors to the rugged heritage of Patagonian ranch life.
experiences.location: Estancia Cerro Guido, Puerto Natales Gateway Area, Patagonia

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort, Torres del Paine. Check-in with a warm welcome amenity — enjoy a glass of premium Carménère wine and a light charcuterie board prepared by the resort chef upon arrival.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome board at resort: artisan cheeses, cured meats, local olives, and fresh sourdough. Paired with Chilean wine or herbal Patagonian tea.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Resort concierge should be notified of late arrival. Keep Day 1 completely relaxed — no early morning obligations the following day to allow jet lag recovery.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late morning start. Sleep in and enjoy a premium resort breakfast with panoramic views of the park. After breakfast, take a gentle orientation walk around the resort grounds and lakeshore — familiarize yourself with the stunning Patagonian landscape, spot local birdlife including Andean condors and flamingos. Meet with the resort's private guide to review and personalize the full trekking itinerary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided introduction hike to a nearby mirador (lookout) accessible from the resort — a moderate 2–3 hour scenic trail offering sweeping views of Lago del Toro and the Paine Massif. This serves as a perfect acclimatization hike before more demanding treks ahead. Return to resort for a full afternoon of relaxation at the spa.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort terrace overlooking the Patagonian steppe. Pre-dinner pisco sour tasting curated by the resort mixologist. Formal welcome dinner at the resort's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet resort breakfast: freshly baked medialunas, smoked salmon, farm eggs cooked to order, seasonal fruit, specialty Chilean coffee and loose-leaf teas.
meals.lunch: Light picnic-style lunch on the trail: gourmet sandwiches, energy bars, fresh fruit, and thermos of hot soup prepared by the resort kitchen.
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — multi-course tasting menu featuring Patagonian king crab, slow-braised guanaco, and local berry desserts. Paired with curated Chilean wine flight.

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. Gear check recommended — ensure all trekking equipment is ready. Resort concierge can arrange any last-minute gear rentals or purchases from Puerto Natales.

day_by_day.morning: Early wake-up at 04:30 for the iconic Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike. Private luxury transfer to the trailhead at Hotel Las Torres. Begin the 4–5 hour guided ascent through lenga beech forest and moraine fields. Arrive at the stunning granite towers at sunrise — witness the legendary alpenglow as the first light turns the towers gold and rose. This is one of Patagonia's most celebrated natural spectacles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend the trail at a relaxed pace, taking time for photography and wildlife spotting — look for pumas, guanacos, and Andean foxes. Return to the resort by early afternoon. Enjoy a restorative soak in the outdoor hot tub with views of the massif, followed by a 60-minute deep-tissue massage at the resort spa.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet evening at the resort. Enjoy the resort library lounge with a curated selection of Patagonian literature and wildlife guides. Private stargazing session on the resort deck with a resident astronomer — Patagonia's remote skies offer extraordinary Milky Way visibility in December.

meals.breakfast: Pre-hike power breakfast at 04:00: protein-rich eggs, avocado toast, granola, and fresh juice. Hot thermos of coffee and tea for the trail.
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch pack delivered to the mirador: artisan wraps, premium trail mix, dark chocolate, and a vacuum flask of hot tomato bisque.
meals.dinner: Intimate candlelit dinner at the resort: grilled Patagonian lamb chops with chimichurri, roasted root vegetables, and a fine Malbec from Mendoza.

day_by_day.notes: Sunrise hike requires very early start — confirm wake-up call with resort the night before. Wear warm layers as temperatures near the towers can drop significantly even in December. Trekking poles strongly recommended for the moraine section.

day_by_day.morning: Departure for the W Trek Multi-Day Hike — Day 1 of 4. Private transfer to the starting point at Lago Grey. Begin the western arm of the W Trek with a guided hike along the shores of Lago Grey toward the Grey Glacier viewpoints. Marvel at the electric-blue ice walls and floating icebergs. The trail winds through native Patagonian forest and open steppe with dramatic mountain backdrops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking toward Refugio Grey — approximately 11 km total for the day. Arrive at the premium glamping or refugio accommodation pre-arranged by the resort. Settle in and enjoy the glacier views from your private accommodation. Optional short afternoon walk to an elevated lookout above the refugio.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset over the Grey Glacier from the refugio terrace. Communal fire pit gathering with fellow trekkers. Pre-arranged premium dinner service at the refugio.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast before departure: eggs, pastries, fresh juice, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch pack: smoked trout wrap, energy bars, mixed nuts, and hot soup in a thermos.
meals.dinner: Premium refugio dinner: hearty Patagonian stew with lamb and root vegetables, crusty bread, and a glass of Chilean red wine. Warm dessert with local calafate berry sauce.

day_by_day.notes: Pack multi-day trekking gear — the resort concierge will have arranged porterage for heavier luggage if desired. Carry a daypack with essentials. Weather can change rapidly — always carry waterproof layers. Accommodation along the W Trek should be pre-booked well in advance, especially for premium options.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek — Day 2. Morning departure from Refugio Grey. Today's highlight: the Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition. Meet expert guides at the Lago Grey embarkation point. Don dry suits and paddle through the icy glacial waters surrounded by towering icebergs calved from the 6 km-wide Grey Glacier. Guides provide fascinating commentary on glaciology and climate impact. This is an extraordinary up-close encounter with one of Patagonia's most dramatic natural features.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from kayaking and continue trekking eastward along the W route toward Refugio Pehoe or Refugio Cuernos. The trail offers sweeping views of the Cuernos del Paine — the dramatic horned peaks that define the park's skyline. Approximately 10–12 km of trekking through varied terrain.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at premium refugio accommodation. Hot shower and change of clothes. Relax on the terrace with views of Lago Nordenskjöld as the evening light plays across the Cuernos. Dinner at the refugio with fellow trekkers.

meals.breakfast: Refugio breakfast: oatmeal with dried fruit, toast with jam and butter, scrambled eggs, and hot beverages.
meals.lunch: Packed kayaking lunch: gourmet energy-dense snacks, sandwiches, hot soup, and chocolate consumed during a scenic break on the glacier lake shore.
meals.dinner: Refugio premium dinner: grilled salmon with Andean herb sauce, quinoa salad, and calafate berry tart for dessert.

day_by_day.notes: Kayaking requires moderate fitness and comfort with cold water environments. Dry suits are provided but ensure you communicate any concerns to guides beforehand. The kayaking segment adds approximately 3–4 hours to the day — plan energy accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek — Day 3. Today's major highlight: Valle del Francés Day Trek. Early start from the refugio and take the catamaran across Lago Nordenskjöld to Refugio Los Cuernos. Begin the ascent into the Valle del Francés — a glacially carved amphitheater of staggering scale. The trail climbs through lenga beech forest into open alpine terrain. Listen for the thunderous crack of hanging glaciers calving from the peaks above.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach the upper valley mirador — one of the most dramatic viewpoints in all of Patagonia, surrounded by hanging glaciers, vertical rock faces, and the iconic Cuernos del Paine. Spend time at the top absorbing the views before beginning the descent. Return to the refugio area by late afternoon. Rest and recover with a warm drink.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the midpoint of the W Trek with a special group dinner. Toast to the journey with a premium bottle of Casillero del Diablo Reserva Privada. Enjoy the long Patagonian December evening light — sunset can occur as late as 22:00, offering extraordinary photography opportunities.

meals.breakfast: Early energizing breakfast: porridge with honey and nuts, boiled eggs, toast, and strong coffee.
meals.lunch: Summit lunch at the mirador: gourmet packed lunch with artisan bread, cured meats, hard cheeses, fruit, and a thermos of hot chocolate.
meals.dinner: Special mid-trek celebratory dinner at the refugio: slow-cooked Patagonian lamb with roasted vegetables, red wine, and a decadent chocolate mousse.

day_by_day.notes: The Valle del Francés is the most physically demanding section of the W Trek. Allow extra time and energy. The upper valley can be windy — secure all loose items. The catamaran crossing is subject to weather conditions; confirm schedule the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek — Day 4 (Final Day). Morning departure toward the eastern arm of the W — the trail to Mirador Las Torres from the western approach. This is a different perspective from Day 3's sunrise hike, approaching through the Valle del Ascencio. The trail passes through beautiful riparian forest and open pampa. Take time to reflect on the journey and appreciate the landscape with fresh eyes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Complete the W Trek at Hotel Las Torres — a landmark achievement. Private luxury vehicle arranged by the resort picks up the group and transfers back to Aegean Bliss Resort. Arrive at the resort to a hero's welcome: chilled champagne, fresh towels, and a drawn bath with Patagonian mineral salts waiting in your suite.
day_by_day.evening: Full resort indulgence evening. Extended session at the resort spa: hot stone massage, steam room, and hydrotherapy pool. Dress for a formal celebratory dinner at the resort's finest dining room.

meals.breakfast: Final trail breakfast: full hot meal at the refugio — eggs, bacon, toast, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Celebratory trail lunch at the Torres viewpoint: premium picnic spread with sparkling water, artisan snacks, and a small bottle of Chandon Patagonia sparkling wine.
meals.dinner: Grand celebratory W Trek completion dinner at the resort: seven-course tasting menu with wine pairing — featuring Patagonian seafood, premium lamb, and an elaborate dessert course. Chef's table experience available on request.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private transfer pickup from Hotel Las Torres in advance. Confirm exact pickup time with resort concierge on Day 6. Post-trek spa treatments should be booked ahead of time to ensure availability.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery day at the resort. Sleep in with no obligations. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast in bed or on your private terrace. Morning yoga session offered by the resort's resident instructor — a gentle flow class designed for post-trekking muscle recovery, held on a deck overlooking the Patagonian steppe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided wildlife safari by 4x4 vehicle through the park's interior roads. Spot guanacos, rheas (ñandús), Andean condors, flamingos, and if lucky, a Patagonian puma. Expert naturalist guide provides in-depth commentary on the park's unique ecosystem. Visit the Laguna Azul area in the park's northeastern sector — a stunning, rarely visited turquoise lake.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Patagonian Asado Dinner experience. Gather around a traditional open fire where the resort's asador has been slow-roasting a whole lamb on a cruz (cross-spit) since the morning. Enjoy the full ceremonial asado experience with chimichurri, grilled vegetables, fresh salads, and premium Patagonian wines under the open sky.

meals.breakfast: Luxurious in-room or terrace breakfast: fresh-squeezed juices, pastries, smoked salmon, eggs Benedict, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Light resort lunch: fresh ceviche, seasonal salad, and sparkling water — keeping appetite for the evening asado.
meals.dinner: Traditional Patagonian Asado: slow-roasted whole lamb (cordero al palo), chorizo, morcilla, grilled provolone, fresh chimichurri, roasted potatoes, and a selection of premium Malbec and Carménère wines.

day_by_day.notes: The wildlife safari is best conducted in the early afternoon when animals are most active near water sources. The asado dinner is a highlight experience — dress warmly as it is held outdoors. This is one of Patagonia's most authentic culinary traditions.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided photography tour of the park's most photogenic locations. Depart at dawn to capture the golden hour light on the Paine Massif. Visit Lago Pehoé for the classic reflection shot of the Cuernos del Paine in the still morning water. Continue to Salto Grande waterfall — a powerful cascade connecting Lago Nordenskjöld and Lago Pehoé, spectacular in December at peak flow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Laguna Verde and Laguna Amarga areas — flamingo habitats in the park's eastern sector. The pink flamingos against the turquoise lagoons with snow-capped peaks behind create extraordinary photographic compositions. Return to resort by mid-afternoon for a relaxed afternoon at leisure.
day_by_day.evening: Private wine and cheese tasting hosted by the resort sommelier. Explore a curated selection of Chilean wines from the Maipo Valley, Colchagua Valley, and Casablanca Valley paired with artisan Patagonian cheeses and local accompaniments. Followed by a quiet dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn light breakfast: energy bars, fruit, and thermos of coffee for the photography tour.
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic at Lago Pehoé: artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, sparkling water, and local pastries enjoyed with the iconic view.
meals.dinner: Resort intimate dinner following the wine tasting: grilled Patagonian trout with lemon caper butter, seasonal vegetables, and a light panna cotta with berry coulis.

day_by_day.notes: Bring a quality camera and tripod for the photography tour — the early morning light is exceptional. The resort can arrange a professional photography guide for guests interested in advanced composition techniques.

day_by_day.morning: Festive Christmas Eve morning. Sleep in and enjoy a special holiday breakfast spread at the resort. Mid-morning guided horseback riding excursion through the Patagonian steppe — a traditional gaucho experience arranged through a local estancia. Ride through open pampa with views of the massif, accompanied by an experienced gaucho guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from horseback riding and enjoy a leisurely afternoon at the resort. Relax by the indoor heated pool or enjoy the resort's outdoor hot tub as temperatures cool. Optional visit to the resort's private art gallery featuring works by Patagonian and Chilean artists.
day_by_day.evening: Special Christmas Eve Gala Dinner at the resort. The resort transforms its dining room into an elegant festive setting. Multi-course Christmas Eve menu featuring the finest Patagonian ingredients. Live acoustic music by a local Chilean musician. Toast the holiday season with vintage Champagne as the long Patagonian summer twilight lingers past 22:00.

meals.breakfast: Christmas Eve special breakfast: festive pastries, smoked salmon blinis, eggs royale, fresh tropical fruit, and mimosas.
meals.lunch: Light estancia-style lunch during the horseback excursion: traditional empanadas, fresh bread, and mate tea prepared gaucho-style.
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve Gala: amuse-bouche, Patagonian king crab bisque, grilled tenderloin with truffle jus, artisan cheese course, and a showstopping bûche de Noël dessert. Vintage Champagne and premium wine pairings throughout.

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve dinner is a signature resort event — formal attire recommended. Book the horseback riding excursion through the resort concierge at least 48 hours in advance. The long summer daylight hours in December make Christmas Eve particularly magical in Patagonia.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas morning at leisure. Enjoy the most indulgent breakfast of the trip on your private terrace — a Christmas morning feast delivered by the resort's butler service. Gift exchange if traveling with companions. Mid-morning, join the resort's optional guided meditation and nature walk — a mindful Christmas morning stroll along the lakeshore, reflecting on the extraordinary journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat excursion on Lago del Toro or Lago Grey — a luxury catamaran charter arranged by the resort. Sail through the glacial waters with Champagne and canapés, approaching the Grey Glacier from the water for a perspective impossible to achieve on foot. Expert guide narrates the glaciology and ecology of the region.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Day farewell dinner — a grand final evening at the resort celebrating both Christmas and the end of an extraordinary Patagonian adventure. The resort's head chef presents a special Christmas tasting menu. Reflect on the highlights of the trip over a final premium wine selection.

meals.breakfast: Christmas morning feast: freshly baked croissants and panettone, smoked salmon, lobster eggs Benedict, fresh berries and cream, Champagne, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Champagne and canapé lunch aboard the private catamaran: lobster medallions, smoked duck, artisan crackers, and a selection of Chilean sparkling wines.
meals.dinner: Christmas Day tasting menu: seven courses featuring the best of Patagonian cuisine — king crab, lamb, local mushrooms, and a grand Christmas dessert platter with calafate sorbet, chocolate fondant, and fresh cream.

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day boat excursion must be booked well in advance — private charters fill quickly during the holiday season. Dress warmly for the boat excursion even in December. Christmas Day is a wonderful opportunity for reflection and gratitude — consider journaling the highlights of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Torres del Paine. Wake early for one last sunrise walk along the resort's private lakeshore trail — a quiet, personal farewell to one of the world's most spectacular landscapes. Watch the first light illuminate the Paine Massif one final time. Return for a leisurely farewell breakfast at the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort after a full morning of relaxation. Private luxury transfer to Puerto Natales or Punta Arenas airport for onward flight connections. The resort concierge will have arranged all luggage handling and transfer logistics.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. If flight timing allows, a final dinner in Puerto Natales is recommended at one of the town's premium restaurants before heading to the airport.

meals.breakfast: Farewell breakfast: full gourmet spread — everything you loved most from the trip, specially curated by the resort chef as a send-off.
meals.lunch: Light in-transit lunch or airport lounge dining in Punta Arenas.
meals.dinner: If time permits before departure: dinner at Restaurante Indio in Puerto Natales — renowned for premium Patagonian lamb and local seafood, or airport lounge dining.

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample transfer time — the drive from Torres del Paine to Puerto Natales is approximately 1.5–2 hours, and to Punta Arenas approximately 4–5 hours. Confirm flight times and arrange transfer accordingly with the resort concierge on Day 11. Consider purchasing local artisan gifts and Patagonian products before departure — the resort boutique or Puerto Natales shops are excellent options.

query: Patagonia hiking Torres del Paine, $4500, 12 days, December 2026
